subject_required: A* Maths (significant pure element) + one science: CS, Further Maths, Biology, Chemistry or Physics
epq_reduction: EPQ not in offer conditions but may be considered in August if places available
excluded_subjects: Use of Mathematics; Core Mathematics (do not satisfy Maths requirement)
additional_conditions: A* Maths must include significant pure element. Must pass practical element of any science A level. Minimum one science subject required.
document_text: Manchester A level entry requires A*A*A including A* in Mathematics, and a minimum of one science subject from Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics. A level Mathematics must include a significant pure element - Use of Mathematics or Core Mathematics does not satisfy this. Applicants must pass the practical element of any science A level taken. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

subject_required: Maths (significant pure element) + one science: CS, Further Maths, Biology, Chemistry or Physics
additional_conditions: Contextual offer drops A*A*A to AAA. GCSE English requirement drops to C/4 for contextual/WP applicants. Must pass practical science element.
document_text: Manchester A level contextual offer is AAA including Mathematics and a minimum of one science subject from Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics. This is two grades below the standard A*A*A offer. A level Mathematics must include a significant pure element. Students eligible for a contextual offer need only GCSE English Language grade C/4 instead of B/6. Check eligibility on the Manchester contextual admissions page.

subject_required: 7 in HL Maths: Analysis and Approaches + one HL science
excluded_subjects: Only HL Maths Analysis and Approaches accepted (not Applications and Interpretation)
additional_conditions: Minimum one HL science: Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry or Biology. Only HL Maths Analysis and Approaches accepted for Maths requirement.
document_text: Manchester IB entry requires 38 points overall with 7,7,6 in Higher Level subjects, including 7 in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. Applicants must study a minimum of one science subject at Higher Level from Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry or Biology. Only Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches is accepted to meet the Maths requirement. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: AAA at Advanced Higher including Maths and science
subject_required: Advanced Higher Maths and a science subject
additional_conditions: Three combinations accepted. Maths of Mechanics accepted for science requirement at AH. English at SCQF level 5 minimum if not at Higher/AH.
document_text: Manchester Scottish entry requires one of: three Advanced Highers AAA including Mathematics and a science; OR two Advanced Highers AA including Maths and a science plus three Highers AAA; OR two Advanced Highers AA including Maths and a science plus two Highers AA in different subjects. Mathematics of Mechanics is accepted to meet the science requirement at Advanced Higher. English not taken at Higher must be at SCQF level 5 minimum (National 5 grade B).

headline_grade: Accepted with 2 A levels including Maths and science
subject_required: 2 A levels including Maths and one science subject
additional_conditions: Requires two A levels including Maths and one science within the qualification. Minimum grade normally same as lowest grade in A level requirements.
document_text: Manchester accepts the Welsh Baccalaureate Advanced Diploma or Advanced Skills Challenge Certificate and requires two A levels including Mathematics and one science subject to be included within it. The minimum grade required will normally be the same as the lowest grade listed in the A level entry requirements. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: D*DD plus A* in A level Maths
subject_required: A level Maths A* required. Second A level or specific BTEC subject needed.
additional_conditions: Engineering BTEC D*DD + A* A level Maths + A in second A level; OR any subject BTEC D*DD + A* A level Maths + A in A level CS, Further Maths, Biology, Chemistry or Physics.
document_text: Manchester BTEC Level 3 National Extended Diploma entry requires D*DD in Engineering plus A* in A level Mathematics and grade A in a second A level; OR D*DD in any subject plus A* in A level Mathematics and grade A in A level Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: D*D plus A* in A level Maths
subject_required: A level Maths A* required. Second A level or specific BTEC subject needed.
additional_conditions: Engineering BTEC D*D + A* A level Maths + A in second A level; OR any subject BTEC D*D + A* A level Maths + A in A level CS, Further Maths, Biology, Chemistry or Physics.
document_text: Manchester BTEC Level 3 National Diploma entry requires D*D in Engineering plus A* in A level Mathematics and grade A in a second A level; OR D*D in any subject plus A* in A level Mathematics and grade A in A level Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: D* plus A*A at A level including A* Maths
subject_required: A level Maths A* + A in a science subject
additional_conditions: Foundation Diploma D* in any subject plus two A levels A*A including A* Maths and A in CS, Further Maths, Biology, Chemistry or Physics.
document_text: Manchester BTEC Level 3 National Foundation Diploma entry requires grade D* in any subject plus two A levels at grades A*A including A* in Mathematics and A in Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: D* plus A*A at A level including A* Maths
subject_required: A level Maths A* + A in a science subject
additional_conditions: Extended Certificate D* in any subject plus two A levels A*A including A* Maths and A in a science subject.
document_text: Manchester BTEC Level 3 National Extended Certificate entry requires grade D* in any subject plus two A levels at grades A*A including A* in Mathematics and A in a science subject (Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry or Physics). GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required. The National Certificate is not accepted.

headline_grade: Same as equivalent BTEC + A* A level Maths
subject_required: A level Maths A* required alongside
additional_conditions: CTEC accepted at same grades as equivalent BTEC. Extended Diploma D*DD, Diploma D*D, plus A* A level Maths and A in science. Certificate not accepted.
document_text: Manchester accepts OCR Cambridge Technical qualifications at the same grades as the equivalent BTEC. Cambridge Technical Extended Diploma D*DD or Diploma D*D, in Engineering plus A* A level Maths and A in a second A level, or in any subject plus A* A level Maths and A in a science subject. The Cambridge Technical Certificate is not accepted. GCSE Maths grade B/6 and GCSE English Language grade B/6 required.

headline_grade: 45 L3 credits at Distinction + A* A level Maths
subject_required: 15 L3 Maths credits at Distinction + A* in A level Maths (pure element)
additional_conditions: QAA-recognised Access in science or engineering subject. Each application considered individually - contact Admissions team.
document_text: Manchester Access to HE Diploma entry requires a QAA-recognised diploma in a science or engineering-related subject with minimum 60 credits, of which 45 credits at Level 3 with Distinction including 15 Level 3 Maths credits at Distinction. Students must also have grade A* in A level Mathematics with a pure element. Each application is considered individually - contact the Undergraduate Admissions team.

excluded_subjects: All T levels not accepted for this course
additional_conditions: Manchester does not accept T levels for the Computer Science programme, though other courses may accept them.
document_text: Manchester does not accept T Levels for entry onto the Computer Science programme. The University does accept T Level qualifications for a number of other courses but not for Computer Science.

additional_conditions: EPQ not part of offer conditions but may be considered in August for applicants narrowly missing grades if places available.
document_text: Manchester recognises the benefits of the EPQ but it will not be included in the conditions of your offer. Applicants are encouraged to mention the EPQ in their personal statement. Some academic Schools may take EPQ performance into account in August for applicants who narrowly miss the entry grades if places are available.

headline_grade: WP Plus: 1 grade lower; WP Plus PLUS: 2 grades lower
excluded_subjects: T levels not eligible for contextual offers
additional_conditions: Course must have standard entry ABB or higher. Predicted grades within 2 grades of minimum. Must complete any interview or aptitude test. T levels not eligible.
document_text: Manchester awards WP, WP Plus or WP Plus PLUS flags based on contextual data. WP Plus applicants usually receive a contextual offer one grade below standard entry requirements. WP Plus PLUS applicants usually receive two grades below. The contextual offer applies only if the course has standard entry requirements of ABB or higher, published subject requirements such as Maths are met, and any interview or aptitude test is completed. Contextual offers do not currently apply to T Level qualifications.

additional_conditions: For applicants in local authority care 3+ months, or with UK refugee status or Ukraine scheme visa. Applied automatically via UCAS.
document_text: Manchester offers a UK refugee and care-experienced offer of two grades below the standard requirements. Eligible applicants are those who have been looked after in local authority care for more than three months, or granted refugee status by the UK government, or issued a UK visa under a Ukraine scheme (Homes for Ukraine, Ukraine Family Scheme or Ukraine Extension Scheme). Applied automatically from the UCAS form. For CS this brings the A*A*A standard offer down two grades. Subject requirements such as Mathematics still apply.

additional_conditions: 2026 cycle criteria listed. 2027 cycle adds free school meals, young adult carers, asylum seekers. Applied automatically. No separate application.
document_text: Manchester contextual admissions eligibility for the 2026 cycle covers UK students under 21 who live in an area of disadvantage or low progression to higher education, or attended a school performing below national average over multiple years, or have been in UK care more than three months, or have UK refugee status including Ukraine scheme visas. For the 2027 cycle Manchester adds free school meals eligibility, young adult carers under 25, and asylum seekers or those with humanitarian protection. Students do not apply separately - information is taken from the UCAS form.

headline_grade: Standard offer despite lower predicted grades
additional_conditions: For WP-flagged applicants whose predicted grades are below minimum entry. Offer made at standard requirements, not reduced.
document_text: Manchester may make an aspirational offer to WP-flagged applicants whose predicted grades for certain courses are lower than the minimum entry criteria, because predicted grades do not always show full academic potential. For example if entry requirements are ABB but predicted grades are BBB, Manchester may still offer a place at the standard ABB offer. This differs from a contextual offer as the grades are not reduced. Certain courses also offer lower GCSE requirements for WP Plus and WP Plus PLUS applicants.
